articles.title: OpenAI and Cursor agree on agent coordinators. They disagree on who runs them.

articles.content: OpenAI opened its Agents API in public beta this month, exposing the harness that powers Codex with managed sessions, tool coordination, and subagent orchestration. On the same day, September 10, Curs... [16915 symbols]
articles.summary: OpenAI and Cursor, two major players in AI-assisted software development, have released their Agents API in public beta and launched Projects to coordinate multiple coding agents around larger software work. While these companies sit at different points in the stack, both converge on the same architecture: a coordinator understands the larger objective and manages the work, while specialized agents execute individual pieces. While the specialized agents do their work, the coordinator can act as a source of truth and guide the most efficient target agent. Hilliary Lipsig, a senior principal site reliability engineer at Red Hat, suggests that multi-agent workflows are the same concept, just in a new part of the technical stack. The problem with the single-agent loop is that maintaining reliability in a single context becomes harder. Multi-agent systems do not guarantee better software quality and increase costs and integration risks.
articles.shortSummary: OpenAI and Cursor both launch separate agent coordination tools, emphasizing the need for multi-agent workflows to ensure reliability and accuracy within complex software environments.

articles.title: When the Cloud Goes Dark: Lessons From the Offpunk Philosophy
articles.description: Explore Offpunk, the movement pushing back on hyperconnectivity — and what rising internet outages and 'right to disconnect' laws mean for how tech pros work, stay resilient and even apply for jobs.
articles.content:
So, your internet is down…

Back a long time ago, my first experience of using computers was on a teletype connected over phone lines to a computer. When I went to university, I took a portable typewr... [5011 symbols]
articles.summary: Developer Lionel Dricot (aka Ploum) has developed the Offpunk philosophy, which believes that the internet has become a prison. The philosophy is opposed to hyperconnectivity and suggests that living without a smart phone is a way to avoid dependence on the digital world. This includes ditching smartphones and switching to a dumb phone, using Bitchat (Bluetooth), the Gemini protocol for accessing remote documents, Tor and encrypted email, and using digital camera instead. The concept also suggests that when the internet goes down due to power cuts or political activity, many websites are powered by cloud services like Amazon, which can cause significant disruption. However, PlouM argues for less connectivity, perhaps switching to mesh network or working in a reduced connectivity environment.
articles.shortSummary: Offpunk philosophy advocates for a more hands-free, offline world, emphasizing essential practices to avoid dependence on internet for work and personal life, despite its dangers from connectivity issues.

articles.title: “Someone will control your systems and your digital future — make sure that someone is you”
articles.description: Pearl Almeida, a cybersecurity expert at Info Tech, has warned that the fact that US multinationals control 85% of the digital storage market poses a serious risk to digital sovereignty.
articles.content: In October of last year, a simple internal computer glitch caused a massive outage of Amazon Web Services (AWS) servers worldwide. What seemed like a routine technical problem quickly turned into a do... [10372 symbols]
articles.summary: Pearse Almeida, Director of Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence Research at Info-Tech Research Group and former CISO with extensive experience in national security, has warned that digital sovereignty is the foundation that defines the global economy, the future, and the balance of power between countries. She suggested that organizations assess their level of digital independence by asking four simple questions: where the data is stored, who can control it, who has the power to shut it down, and if it is safe to switch providers if needed. In the European cloud services market, U.S. companies hold 85% of the sector and just three major tech companies, Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, control almost 70%. Industry estimates suggest that between 80% and 90% of all digital infrastructure in Europe is in the hands of foreign companies. AlmeIDA also highlighted the vulnerability of this dependence on technology from other countries. To address this issue, public sector has taken action, including France's announcement to replace tools like Microsoft Teams and Zoom with a national videoconferencing platform by 2027 and the European Commission's awarding of 180 million euros in sovereign cloud contracts.
articles.shortSummary: The internet outage caused by Amazon's AWS outage highlighted the urgent need for companies to assess digital sovereignty and ensure their operations and data are safe and effective.

articles.summary: How to Compare Disaster Recovery Options to Healthcare Providers can help providers navigate between patient safety and clinical service continuity, and realistic recovery-time objectives (RTO) and recovery-point objective (RPO) targets. Compare recovery options on restoration testing, cyber resilience, interoperability, staffing demands, and infrastructure dependencies, not backup capacity. On-premises, cloud, hybrid, and managed approaches each have tradeoffs and many healthcare organizations will benefit from combining them by workload tier. The American Hospital Association's 2025 cybersecurity review also reviews breaches and defensive measures affecting healthcare. The HHS Office of Inspector General's fiscal year 2025 information-security review rated the department’s program “Not Effective” for the sixth consecutive year and placed its recovery metrics below the “Managed and Measurable” maturity level. Healthcare buyers should verify the proposed scope, contractual controls, recovery targets, testing responsibilities, and total cost for managed services and cloud-native tools.
articles.shortSummary: Apex Technology Services advises healthcare providers to prioritize patient safety and clinical service continuity over overall recovery options, focusing on operational resilience, interoperability, and managed recovery targets.

articles.summary: Ransomware group known as Pear has reportedly listed Indroj Medical Group Inc., a U.S. healthcare organization, on its leak site. The claim surfaced on September 24–25, 2026 and is being tracked as an unverified ransomware/extortion allegation. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services’ NPI Registry lists Indrooj MedicalGroup Inc. under NPI 1184666570 and classifies it as a multi-specialty/internal-medicine organization. However, the existence of the organization does not verify Pear’s claim that it was compromised. The NPI registry contains publicly accessible provider information and does not determine whether a healthcare provider is licensed or credentialed. However there is no independently verified evidence in the available reporting establishing what data was accessed, how many people were affected, or whether ransomware actually disrupted Indroroj’S systems.
articles.shortSummary: Pear's unverified ransomware claim against Indroj Medical Group Inc.
